claims: The University of Michigan men’s basketball team has won one NCAA National Championship.
The University of Michigan men’s basketball team defeated Seton Hall 80–79 in overtime in 1989.
The Wolverines appeared in seven NCAA championship games in 1965, 1976, 1989, 1992, 1993, 2013, and 2018.
The final score of the 1989 NCAA Championship was Michigan 80, Seton Hall 79 in overtime.
Steve Fisher was the interim coach of the 1989 NCAA Championship team.
Glen Rice was the Most Outstanding Player of the 1989 NCAA Championship.
Glen Rice scored 31 points in the 1989 NCAA Championship game.
Rumeal Robinson scored 21 points in the 1989 NCAA Championship game.
The University of Michigan men’s basketball team made Final Four appearances in 1964, 1965, 1976, 1989, 1992, 1993, 2013, and 2018.
The University of Michigan men’s basketball team lost the 1965 NCAA championship game to UCLA.
The University of Michigan men’s basketball team lost the 1976 NCAA championship game to Indiana.
The University of Michigan men’s basketball team lost the 1992 NCAA championship game to Duke.
The University of Michigan men’s basketball team lost the 1993 NCAA championship game to North Carolina.
The University of Michigan men’s basketball team lost the 2013 NCAA championship game to Louisville.
The University of Michigan men’s basketball team lost the 2018 NCAA championship game to Villanova.
The NCAA vacated the 1992 and 1993 Final Four appearances of the University of Michigan men’s basketball team due to sanctions.
The 1992 and 1993 championship game losses were by the "Fab Five."
The 1989 University of Michigan men’s basketball team averaged 91.7 points per game.
